label: measured, n=73 (3-point large-file probe + 10-file checkpoint + 60-file Tier A full run), single machine, mixed parallelism (see parallelism_at_measurement per record), NEVER a percentile
note_on_methodology: The 3 probe files ran at parallelism=1 (fully sequential, isolated). The 10 checkpoint files ran at parallelism=2 (two concurrent workers). elapsed_s for the checkpoint batch may be modestly inflated by contention between the two concurrent workers; peak_rss_bytes for the checkpoint batch was captured via the worker's own getrusage self-report printed at the time (not independently cross-checked by an external poller, unlike the probe batch). 2026-08-15 addendum: the 60-file Tier A run (batch tier_a_full_2025_08_15_night) added per-file swap_out_bytes tracking via /proc/vmstat delta; swap_in_bytes and mem_available_at_start_bytes were computed per-file in-process but not persisted to disk -- an implementation gap, not a measurement absence -- so those two fields are null on every record in this batch. Only swap_out_bytes (and its 0-value absence) is reliable for this batch. Exactly one file (in.hsbc.hsbcindia, the largest, processed first under descending order) had nonzero swap_out: 1458MB.

records.swap_caveat: Added 2026-08-15 (later same night): swap state was not captured at the time this record was measured. Free-memory checks around this period showed ~3.1GB resident in swap; pswpout is a cumulative kernel counter, so this record's elapsed_s may include swap I/O and cannot be retrospectively cleaned. Not recomputed -- dated caveat per repo convention, not a correction.
